evals.prompt: faz a versão narrada desse guia do cache http pra eu ouvir indo pro trabalho
evals.expected_output: A PT-BR narration script for one voice, written for the ear from the guide: spoken map, core idea in the first 30 seconds, one part per main concept with a re-entry line, a recall question closing each part, no tables, code, digits, URLs or parentheses, and the response table and header syntax replaced by plain spoken explanation.
expectations: The core idea of the guide is stated within the first 80 words
Each part starts with 'Parte N de M' written in words, followed by a re-entry line that names what the part builds on
Every part ends with exactly one recall question followed by its answer
No header syntax is read literally (no 'max-age=31536000', no 'If-None-Match' spelled as code)
Every factual claim in the script is in the source guide, and all three main concepts are present
At least one dense element of the guide (the response table or the file name with a hash) is spoken as plain explanation or pointed to the written guide

evals.prompt: quero ouvir como podcast, com dois apresentadores, só a parte do no-cache vs no-store e da etiqueta de versão
evals.expected_output: A two-host PT-BR script (Guia and Curioso). The Curioso asks a deep question before each explanation and voices the no-cache misconception, which the Guia corrects. No banter. The key sentence comes right after a voice change.
expectations: The second host speaks within the first three lines
The second host voices the misconception that no-cache means do not store, and the first host corrects it
Deleting every line of the second host removes at least one question or misconception that matters
No line is banter, a joke, or a bare agreement ('Legal!', 'Exato!')
Only the requested concepts are covered, and no fact is added

evals.prompt: me dá um resumo em áudio bem curto disso, tipo 1 minuto, pra revisar antes da reunião
evals.expected_output: A single-part PT-BR review script of about 160 words: core idea first, the three concepts in one or two sentences each, one recall question, one takeaway.
expectations: The script has between 130 and 200 spoken words
The core idea is in the first two sentences
All three main concepts are named
It ends with one takeaway sentence
